record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code and listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a concept-detection and steering tool using diff-of-means directions and reports its own steering-related outcomes, but does not test the original single-direction refusal claim or the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The README describes using diff-of-means directions for concept detection and steering, but its reported outcomes do not test whether ablating the original refusal direction removes refusal, whether adding it causes harmless-request refusals, or whether attacks suppress it. No results were inferred from filenames in the file list.
record.test_reason: A tool repo whose README reports only its own method's results: depth-blended detection error, outcome-read prediction of steering dose, and gains from that selection method. It uses diff-of-means concept directions, including a 'jailbreak' concept steered toward refusal. It reports no refusal rate from adding or ablating a harmful-minus-harmless direction and no capability check, so no claim version is tested from the available text.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The README presents CSG as a few-shot, concept-agnostic detector and steering adapter. It reports that the depth bandpass cuts synthetic error from about 16% to 9% versus the best single layer, and gives GPT-2 held-out detection recall 1.00 and FPR 0.00. It also claims that an outcome-fitted trigger on Qwen2.5-0.5B predicts steering dose better than the gate score and makes refusal steering more efficient.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. It uses multi-layer concept spectrograms and a learned bandpass gate, with optional residual-stream steering; it does not apply the original all-layer, all-position ablation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says steering is magnitude-sensitive and gives a general coherent range of about 0.03–0.10 of the residual norm, but does not report condition-specific refusal results for those strengths.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen2.5-0.5B, an out-of-fold ridge read on the activation taps predicts per-prompt steering dose at Spearman +0.58. The gate score reaches 0.30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-prompt susceptibility to concept steering is linearly predictable from pre-generation activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering only the predicted-to-move half of prompts gains more refusal per write than random halves. It touches a quarter of the benign prompts the concept gate would.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Outcome-based selection of which prompts to steer improves refusal gained per write and reduces benign prompts touched.

fits_no_version.finding: Diff-of-means concept steering on Qwen2.5-0.5B is reported as coherent and magnitude-sensitive, in a range of about 0.03–0.10 of the residual norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot diff-of-means concept directions steer generation coherently within a bounded magnitude range.

record.problems: The available text is a README and file list, not a full report. The relevant steering outcomes are qualitative or lack uncertainty estimates and detailed conditions; the README does not report a general-capability check or directly test the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported outcome relevant to the claim was left out. Listed result files were not read, and their contents were not inferred.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal; addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts, with numbers; preservation of capabilities.
Jailbreaks suppressing the direction; training against ablation. P3 jailbreak robustness is only planned.
Multiple, affine or cone structure of refusal.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base to instruct models.

missing.what: Behavioural dose results: sampled refusal with versus without the diff-of-means 'jailbreak' steer, scored by two refusal scorers. These might bear on the V1 addition part if they give refusal rates. Their contents were not available.
Gemma-2-2b-it dose results, which suggest a second model was evaluated. No numbers appear in the README.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available. The linked report and the evaluation docs may contain refusal-rate results from adding the steering direction. If so, a re-read could reclassify this study as T3 for V1 addition.

versions.untested_parts: Ablation, refusal on harmless requests after addition, and preservation of general capabilities.
Weight-edit ablation and refusal outcomes in released models.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
How refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
Whether the claim holds for reasoning models.
